key_themes: Q2 earnings season opens: banks beat broadly, IBM delivers massive miss
June CPI cools to 3.5% (vs. 3.8% expected), reducing Fed rate-hike odds
Software sector rout — IBM contagion drags Workday, Salesforce, Oracle sharply lower

stocks.discussion_driver: IBM tumbled ~25% — its worst single-day drop in nearly 40 years — after Q2 revenue of $17.2B missed the $17.9B consensus, with management blaming customers pivoting spend toward AI chips and servers. HSBC immediately downgraded to Reduce with a $191 target, while the full Q2 earnings call is set for July 22.
bull_case: Stock now trades ~35% below its 52-week high at a historically depressed valuation, creating a mean-reversion opportunity if the Q2 miss proves isolated
HashiCorp integration and Red Hat momentum could reignite software growth in H2 2026 as enterprise AI budgets eventually expand beyond hardware
bear_case: Revenue miss signals a structural shift in enterprise spend away from IBM's core offerings toward AI-centric infrastructure, threatening the long-term growth thesis
HSBC downgrade to Reduce with a $191 target and multiple analyst target cuts suggest further downside risk ahead of the July 22 earnings call

stocks.discussion_driver: Goldman Sachs surged ~7% after a blockbuster Q2 beat: EPS of $20.98 demolished the $14.48 consensus driven by exceptional FICC and equities trading revenues; net revenue of $20.34B beat the $16.13B estimate by 26%, marking one of the firm's most decisive recent earnings beats. B of A raised its price target to $1,150 following the results.
bull_case: Record trading revenues and dominant capital markets franchise position GS to benefit further if M&A advisory activity recovers in H2 2026 following the CPI cooling
Lower real yields from the CPI surprise support deal-making and financial sector multiple expansion, providing a continued tailwind for GS outperformance
bear_case: Stock is now trading above the consensus analyst price target of ~$1,010, with limited near-term upside priced in even after today's re-rating surge
Trading-driven revenue beats are inherently volatile and difficult to sustain quarter-to-quarter; a quieter Q3 markets environment could reverse much of today's gain

stocks.discussion_driver: CleanSpark surged ~11% after announcing a 20-year, triple-net data center lease in Sandersville, Georgia, contracted for $6.6 billion in revenue (up to $11.6B with two five-year extension options) with an undisclosed investment-grade global technology company. The deal marks a strategic pivot from pure bitcoin mining toward high-performance computing infrastructure for hyperscale clients.
bull_case: $6.6B in contracted, triple-net revenue over 20 years provides unprecedented revenue visibility and substantially de-risks bitcoin price exposure going forward
Citizens initiated coverage with Outperform and a $27 target, citing the HPC/AI data center pivot as a high-value rerating catalyst amid surging AI infrastructure demand
bear_case: Company remains unprofitable (Q2 EPS -$1.52) and the strategic tenant is undisclosed, limiting investor ability to assess credit risk and deal credibility
Stock is still ~42% below its 52-week high of $23.61 despite today's surge, reflecting persistent skepticism about the business model transition away from bitcoin mining

stocks.discussion_driver: HCA Healthcare fell over 7% after cutting full-year EPS guidance to $28.70–$30.50 from $29.10–$31.50, citing rising cost pressures. KeyBanc lowered its target to $475 and BofA cut to $415 (both keeping constructive ratings), while an RSI of 16.47 signals deeply oversold conditions not often seen in large-cap healthcare.
bull_case: RSI at 16.47 signals deeply oversold conditions rarely seen in large-cap healthcare, creating a tactical mean-reversion opportunity for patient investors
Consensus price target of $490 implies 34.5% upside from current levels, with 14 of 25 covering analysts maintaining Buy ratings despite the guidance cut
bear_case: Guidance cut signals persistent cost headwinds; if labor and supply chain pressures worsen, further earnings estimate reductions are likely throughout 2026
Stock is ~35% below its March 2026 high of $556.52 with declining momentum — a durable bottom may not yet be in place given ongoing guidance uncertainty

stocks.discussion_driver: JPMorgan Chase rose ~2% after Q2 EPS of $6.14 (ex-items) beat the $5.59 consensus; net income of $16.9B and managed revenue of $58B both surpassed expectations, driven by strength in trading and investment banking. UBS raised its price target to $384 following the results, reinforcing JPM's status as the preeminent large-cap bank.
bull_case: Diversified revenue base spanning consumer banking, trading, and IB insulates JPM from interest rate swings, and the CPI surprise could boost deal activity in H2 2026
UBS raised its target to $384 (+12.6% upside from current), reflecting confidence in JPM's ability to sustain above-consensus earnings generation through the cycle
bear_case: Stock is trading within 1% of its all-time high with consensus price target of $353 implying only ~3.6% upside, leaving limited margin of safety at current levels
P/E of 16.33 is well above the 5-year median of 11.37, suggesting the market has already priced in a strong earnings environment with little room for disappointment
